intro: A Portland mandolinist and his bluegrass band.
story: Caleb Klauder's bluegrass band played Pickathon in 2001, and its music soundtracked a Food Network trip through Portland the next year. Klauder went on to found Foghorn Stringband, and the Caleb Klauder Country Band made Dangerous Me's and Poisonous You's and Western Country before its first Mountain Stage appearance in April 2012.

The Clumsy Lovers came together in Vancouver in 1993 from the original lineup of the Paperboys, and they were a touring band by 2001, playing more than 270 shows in 2002. Nettwerk Records released After the Flood in 2004 and Smart Kid a year later. The band has since counted more than 2,500 performances.

intro: A founding fiddler of new acoustic music and his guitarist.
story: Darol Anger, a founding member of the Turtle Island String Quartet, brought guitarist Scott Nygaard to Pickathon in 2001, the year his album Now Hear This came out. Nygaard had played with Tim O'Brien's O'Boys and with Laurie Lewis in Grant Street, and the two later built Republic of Strings, a young fiddle ensemble whose Compass Records debut had Lewis and Sara Watkins of Nickel Creek as guests.

intro: A Portland old-time band with a punk crowd.
story: The Dickel Brothers, a Portland string band that dressed in old-fashioned hats and suits, put its records out on Seattle's Empty Records, a punk label, and drew a rowdy punk-show crowd. Volume One and Volume Two were both on Empty, and No Depression put Volume One somewhere between reverent and slapstick. The band was back at Pickathon in 2005.

intro: A Portland bluegrass and string band.
story: Harebrained, a bluegrass and string band, played Pickathon in 2001, the third of four straight years from 1999 to 2002.
Jackstraw, a Portland bluegrass quartet formed in 1994, was on the 2001 bill and has come back more often than most bands, through 2022.

intro: A Bay Area bluegrass singer, fiddler and songwriter.
story: Laurie Lewis, whose "Who Will Watch the Home Place" was the IBMA's song of the year in 1994, played Pickathon in 2001 with Tom Rozum. That year the IBMA gave its collaborative recording award to Follow Me Back to the Fold, a tribute to women in bluegrass that carries her name. The Hazel and Alice Sessions, with the Right Hands, was nominated for the 2017 Grammy for Best Bluegrass Album, and O California!, her 25th album, came out in February 2026.

intro: A Portland country and folk singer.
story: Lynn Conover, a Portland singer billed with Susannah Weaver in 2001, was on the Pickathon bill five times between 1999 and 2006.
Pig Iron, a Portland bluegrass band, played Pickathon in 2001. Caleb Klauder, who went on to found Foghorn Stringband, lists it among the bands he toured with early on, alongside Colobo.

Sam Hill, a Portland bluegrass band built on mandolinist Jeff Smith's traditional-sounding originals, played Pickathon in 2001, the year it self-released its third CD, Haunted by a Memory. Laurie Lewis, also on the 2001 bill, had recorded Smith's "Hard Luck & Trouble," the title track of the band's second CD. Smith has said the model was the Bill Monroe of the late 1950s.

Shorty and the Mustangs formed in 1996, when a Texas-raised musician known as Big Tex called some friends and they dug out old Bob Wills and Ernest Tubb records to try western swing. They played Pickathon in 2001, later turned to original songs, and made Too Late Too Soon at Panther Studios in Portland, out in September 2022.

Terry Robb, who befriended John Fahey in the early 1980s and later produced and played on most of Fahey's late albums, signed with Portland's Burnside Records in 1994. He played Pickathon in 2001, a year after Heart Made of Steel, and followed with When I Play My Blues Guitar in 2002. His album CrissCross came out in October 2024.
